previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and a history of renal transplant failure was admitted with acute chest pain radiating to the neck and shoulders, worsened by breathing and movement. Evaluation revealed a new pericardial effusion on echocardiogram and CT, with no signs of tamponade or pulmonary embolism. Cardiac enzymes were negative, ruling out myocardial infarction. The effusion was attributed to pericarditis, possibly lupus-related or viral. She was treated with a prednisone increase to 30mg daily, resulting in symptom improvement. Her warfarin was held due to rising INR and risk of hemorrhagic complications, and vitamin K was given. Peritoneal dialysis was optimized with shorter dwells to improve clearance. Fevers and leukocytosis resolved without evidence of infection. She was discharged home hemodynamically stable, on a prednisone taper, restarted warfarin at 3mg, and with follow-up plans for rheumatology and nephrology.
